acme_ops: Hi team — we just received our March invoice and it's ~18% higher than our local SDK estimator. Nothing changed in our app, can you help investigate?

alex_support: Sorry to hear that — can you share a curl/python repro and the estimator output you saw? Any request IDs from the invoice items would help.

acme_ops: Repro below. SDK (python) shows ~820 tokens, invoice shows 980 for the same request id 1798-inv-7882.
acme_ops: ```python
from redwood import Client
cli = Client(api_key="REDACTED")
payload = {"model":"redwood-13B","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are helpful."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the quarterly metrics."}]}
resp = cli.chat.create(**payload)
print(resp.token_estimate)  # -> 820
```

sara_billing: Thanks. Can you paste the full raw request/response headers (no PII) and the invoice line item (id + token count)?

acme_ops: Invoice line: `1798-inv-7882: 980 tokens`
acme_ops: Raw request headers attached: `X-Redwood-Trace: t-7a3b`, `X-Redwood-Prefill: v1`

alex_support: Noted. Two things to check: 1) are you using streaming/resume? 2) does your SDK estimate include server-injected prefill or KV cache prefixes? Our estimator tries to mirror client-visible prompt only.

acme_ops: We're not doing resume. We do enable the SDK's `prefill_cache=True` to speed up repeated prompts.

ryan_eng: tagging in — from infra side. The platform can insert an opaque prefill blob for KV cache warmups and routing metadata. Historically that added a small token delta, but it should be visible in server-side meter logs. Can you share one full request_id and I'll pull the backend trace?

acme_ops: Request id: `req_20260317_9f3b` (same as invoice trace).

metering-bot: Backend meter event for req_20260317_9f3b -> prompt_tokens: 732, completion_tokens: 248, total: 980, injected_prefix_tokens: 134, source: gateway-prefill-v2.

ryan_eng: OK that matches invoice total 980. The SDK estimator (820) only counted the visible prompt_tokens (732) + completion (88?) — mismatch because it didn't include the injected_prefix_tokens (134) the gateway added for KV prefill + routing metadata.

alex_support: Two follow-ups: 1) SDK should warn when `prefill_cache=True` that server-side prefill may add tokens. 2) We'll open an internal task to surface injected token counts in the response headers so estimators can replicate.

acme_ops: Is there a temporary workaround so our billing estimate aligns? We need to forecast spend accurately for next quarter.

ryan_eng: Short-term: add +134 tokens to your estimator for calls that set `prefill_cache=True` and include the `X-Redwood-Prefill` header in the request. Longer-term: we'll add `X-Redwood-Metering-Injected: <n>` header on responses.

sara_billing: I've flagged billing to treat an adjustment if this caused a surprise spike for a paying customer. If you want, send the invoice id and we'll open a credit review.

acme_ops: Appreciate it. For the repro, should we switch off `prefill_cache` until the estimator update lands?

ryan_eng: That will remove the injected prefill tokens. If your latency tolerance allows it, yes. Otherwise use the +134 fudge factor until we push the header update (ETA 2 weeks).

alex_support: Filed support ticket #SUP-2026-395. We'll follow up with engineering updates and the header rollout plan. :thumbsup:

acme_ops: Thanks all — the quick explanation helps a lot.

ryan_eng: One more note for the team: the injected prefix size varies by model and prompt length; the 134 value was specific to this trace. We'll publish a small doc explaining how to compute conservative upper bounds for prefill overhead.
